parts.label: a
parts.technique: Bias of an estimator (E(2X̄) for discrete uniform parameter)
parts.reason: Involves E(X) of a general discrete random variable and the concept of bias of an estimator, neither of which appear in any 9MA0 statement; S4.1 explicitly excludes calculation of mean of discrete random variables.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Point estimation using sample mean for discrete uniform parameter
parts.reason: Relies on the E(X) relationship from part (a) and estimator theory not present in any statement; discrete uniform distribution mean/estimation is not covered.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Chi-squared goodness-of-fit/independence contribution calculation
parts.reason: Chi-squared test statistic and contingency table analysis are not mentioned anywhere in the 9MA0 statements (S5 only covers binomial proportion and normal mean tests, and correlation coefficient interpretation).

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Chi-squared test of independence
parts.reason: No statement covers chi-squared tests; S5.1-S5.3 restrict hypothesis testing to binomial proportion, normal mean, and correlation coefficient interpretation only.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Spearman's rank correlation coefficient
parts.reason: Spearman's rank correlation is not mentioned in any statement; S5.1 only discusses the product moment correlation coefficient (PMCC), and S5.1/exclusions restrict correlation coefficient calculation to PMCC context, not Spearman's.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Hypothesis test on Spearman's rank correlation coefficient
parts.reason: Testing on Spearman's coefficient is not within S5.1, which is specific to PMCC (ρ); no statement covers rank correlation tests.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Tied ranks in Spearman's coefficient
parts.reason: Relates to Spearman's rank correlation methodology which is entirely absent from the specification statements.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: in spec
parts.reason: question dropped: other parts out of spec

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Chi-squared goodness-of-fit test for uniform distribution
parts.reason: Chi-squared testing is not covered by any statement; S2.4 explicitly limits significance tests to those in Section 5 (binomial proportion, normal mean, correlation coefficient), none of which is chi-squared.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Chi-squared goodness-of-fit test with grouped data
parts.reason: Same reasoning as (b): chi-squared tests are outside the scope of any 9MA0 statement.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Critique of sampling method using prior chi-squared conclusion
parts.reason: The required advice depends on the conclusion reached in the out-of-spec chi-squared test in part (c), so this part only makes sense after an out-of-spec part; also involves interpreting chi-squared results for uniformity of digits, not covered by any statement.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: in spec
parts.reason: question dropped: other parts out of spec

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Hypothesis test for difference of two population means (large sample, unknown variance via sample estimates)
parts.reason: S5.3 only covers a test for the mean of a single Normal distribution with known/given/assumed variance; testing the difference between two independent sample means is not covered by any statement.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Justification via Central Limit Theorem for large samples
parts.reason: S5.3 explicitly excludes 'Knowledge of the Central Limit Theorem or other large sample approximations', which is exactly what this part requires.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Approximate distribution of sample mean from Poisson distribution (CLT)
parts.reason: Poisson distribution is never mentioned in any statement, and use of CLT/large sample approximations for sample means is explicitly excluded by S5.3.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Confidence interval for Poisson mean using normal approximation
parts.reason: Poisson distribution and confidence intervals generally are not covered by any 9MA0 statement.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Probability calculation involving independent confidence intervals
parts.reason: Depends on the out-of-spec confidence interval concept established in part (b), and confidence intervals are not a topic in any statement.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Sum of independent Normal random variables
parts.reason: While the Normal distribution itself is covered by S4.2, no statement mentions combining/summing independent normal random variables to form a new normal distribution; S4.2 only covers using N(μ,σ²) as a model and finding probabilities for a single variable, not linear combinations.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Linear combination of two different independent Normal random variables
parts.reason: Same as (a): combining multiple independent normal variables (of different distributions) into a total distribution is not covered by S4.2 or any other statement.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Distribution theory: linear combination of normal random variables, solving resulting equation for n
parts.reason: Requires deriving the distribution of a defined linear combination of normal variables and solving a quadratic from a standardised value; this combination/derivation technique is not covered by any statement (S4.2 explicitly excludes derivation-type work and doesn't address combinations of random variables).
